title: Will at least 5 non-passengers be linked to the MV Hondius hantavirus outbreak before August 2026?

orchestrator.premortem: The consensus may be missing a Saint Helena amplification scenario: 30 passengers disembarked April 24 without restrictions. One (Swiss, confirmed positive) and possibly others were in incubation. The

reflection.diagnosis: Forecast is ~16x too high. P(>=5)=0.24 is logically incompatible with the Manifold market P(>=1)=0.278 (137 bettors, $13k volume). Under any reasonable count distribution, P(>=5) given P(>=1)=0.278 is 0.5-5%, not 24%. The forecast failed to check prediction markets, overestimated expected secondary cases (2-4 household from Saint Helena with zero confirmed after 24+ days), dismissed negative surveillance results as a mere -0.02 adjustment, and used an irrelevant base rate ('appointment/health' 36%). The sub-agents all shared the same upward bias and their tight convergence (0.18-0.20) was interpreted as bearing increased epistemic weight rather than as a bias signal.

vault_changes.what: Create a 'market-anchor-rule.md' in the vault requiring: (1) Before issuing any threshold forecast (>=n), search prediction markets (Polymarket, Manifold, Metaculus) for related questions at any threshold. (2) Report the market price of the closest match. (3) If the forecast implies P(>=n) > P(>=1) * 0.2 for the market's equivalent P(>=1), provide explicit justification. (4) For count-threshold questions, model the count distribution explicitly (Poisson/NB/two-point) anchored to market prices and document the implied tail probability.
vault_changes.why: This error would have been caught immediately by checking P(>=5) vs P(>=1). The forecast prompt even lists this failure mode but no mechanism enforces it. A concrete rule with mathematical constraints prevents recurrence.

vault_changes.what: Create a 'negative-surveillance-evidence.md' note codifying the principle: when active surveillance with broad testing capacity returns zero cases over a surveillance window longer than the incubation period, this is strong evidence against ongoing transmission — not a minor adjustment. Anchor the probability to 1 / (1 + surveillance-days / incubation-period) as a heuristic, and require explicit defense of any expected case count above what surveillance has already ruled out.
vault_changes.why: The forecast acknowledged negative test results on KLM attendant, Singapore contacts, and US passenger but treated this as a -0.02 disconfirmation adjustment. With 24+ days of multinational surveillance returning zero non-passenger cases, this should have been the dominant signal, not an afterthought.

vault_changes.what: Add a 'sub-agent-debiasing.md' procedure: (1) When sub-agents converge within ±0.03, trigger a mandatory devil's-advocate agent tasked with arguing for the opposite extreme. (2) If the devil's-advocate produces a value that would be a better trade against the market (i.e., would yield positive expected value from the opposite side), reduce weight on the consensus by at least 30%. (3) Record the convergence width and the devil's-advocate result in the forecast metadata.
vault_changes.why: The three sub-agents converged tightly at 0.18-0.20 (within 0.02), which the forecast noted as a shared-bias risk but then paradoxically increased base-rate weight rather than correcting downward. A structured debiasing procedure would surface the market inconsistency and prevent this.

vault_changes.what: Create a 'base-rate-matching.md' guide on selecting reference classes: (1) Prefer categories matched on causal structure (zoonotic spillover, H2H transmission efficiency of the specific pathogen) over broad topic labels. (2) A category like 'appointment/health' with 36% base rate is uninformative for a question about a specific Andes virus H2H outbreak. Document why the category was chosen and what it would take for it to shift. (3) When the base rate conflicts with market prices, give market prices at least 3x weight by default.
vault_changes.why: The forecast anchored a third of its weight (35%) to an irrelevant 36% base rate from a poorly matched category. A structured matching guide would prevent this category of error.

reasoning: Anchored to Manifold market price of 27.8% for >=1 non-passenger case (137 bettors). Under a negative binomial model with moderate overdispersion (r=0.5), P(>=5) = 0.008; under extreme overdispersion (r=0.2), P(>=5) = 0.052. Wikipedia page (through May 18) confirms zero confirmed non-passenger cases after 24+ days of international surveillance. The 30 Saint Helena disembarkees (April 24) have had no confirmed onward transmission despite active monitoring. The KLM stewardess tested negative May 8
